```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

summarize_section <- function(section_data) {
  # Check if required columns exist in the data
  required_columns <- c("bone.level", "element", "count")
  if (!all(required_columns %in% colnames(section_data))) {
    stop("section_data must contain columns: bone.level, element, and count")
  }

  # Check if the count column contains lists
  if (is.list(section_data$count[[1]])) {
    # Unnest the count column if it contains lists
    section_data <- section_data %>%
      unnest(count)
  }

  # Group by bone.level and element, then summarize the total count
  level_summary <- section_data %>%
    group_by(bone.level, element) %>%
    summarise(total = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

  # Return the summarized data
  return(level_summary)
}

# Example usage:
 summarize_section(same_data)
```

```{r}
# Load the necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# =============================================================================
# 1. Prepare the Data: Unnest and Rename the Columns
# =============================================================================

prepare_bone_data <- function(data) {
  # Unnest the list columns together so that each row is one bone record.
  bone_data <- data %>%
    unnest(cols = c(bone.level, element, count))
  
  # Rename columns to standard names:
  bone_data <- bone_data %>%
    rename(
      hierarchical_level = bone.level,  # numeric level
      bone_name = element               # bone name
    ) %>%
    # Make sure that the count column is numeric
    mutate(count = as.numeric(count))
  
  return(bone_data)
}

# =============================================================================
# 2. Summarize a Section: Group by Hierarchical Level and Bone Name
# =============================================================================

summarize_section <- function(bone_data, section) {
  section_data <- bone_data %>% filter(section == section)
  
  # Group by the numeric hierarchical_level and the bone name, then sum counts.
  level_summary <- section_data %>%
    group_by(hierarchical_level, bone_name) %>%
    summarise(total = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
  
  return(level_summary)
}

# =============================================================================
# 3. Main Analysis Function
# =============================================================================

analyze_bone_levels <- function(data, sections_order, target_threshold = "Level A") {
  # Step 1: Prepare the data
  bone_data <- prepare_bone_data(data)
  
  # Step 2: Assign each bone to a section.
  # Adjust these rules to your naming conventions.
  bone_data <- bone_data %>%
    mutate(section = case_when(
      grepl("Skull", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Skull",
      grepl("Humerus|Radius|Ulna", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Arms",
      grepl("Vertebra", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Vertebrae",
      grepl("Thorax", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Thorax",
      grepl("Shoulder", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Shoulder",
      grepl("Hand", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Hands",
      grepl("Pelvic", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Pelvic",
      grepl("Leg", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Legs",
      grepl("Foot", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Foot",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ))
  
  # Step 3: For each section in sections_order, get summaries at the pure minimum
  # level and at the target threshold. (We assume lower numeric values mean more
  # restrictive; e.g., 1 is the pure minimum.)
  
  report <- map(sections_order, function(sec) {
    sec_summary <- summarize_section(bone_data, sec)
    
    # If no records were found for the section, return a message:
    if(nrow(sec_summary) == 0) {
      return(list(
        section = sec,
        message = "No data for this section",
        pure_minimum = NULL,
        target_threshold = NULL,
        differences = NULL
      ))
    }
    
    # Determine the minimum hierarchical level (the pure minimum) for the section.
    min_level <- min(as.numeric(sec_summary$hierarchical_level), na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Determine the target threshold.
    # If the user passed a character like "Level A", then we map that to one level above
    # the minimum. (You might choose a different rule.)
    target_thr <- if (is.character(target_threshold)) {
      if (target_threshold == "Level A") {
        min_level + 1
      } else {
        # For a string like "Level 3", remove "Level " and convert.
        as.numeric(gsub("Level ", "", target_threshold))
      }
    } else {
      # Otherwise assume it's numeric.
      target_threshold
    }
    
    # Get the summary at the pure minimum level
    pure_min <- sec_summary %>% filter(as.numeric(hierarchical_level) == min_level)
    # And get the summary at the target threshold (if any data exist at that level)
    target <- sec_summary %>% filter(as.numeric(hierarchical_level) == target_thr)
    
    # Compute the differences: bones that appear in the target summary but not in pure minimum.
    diff_summary <- anti_join(target, pure_min, by = "bone_name")
    
    list(
      section = sec,
      pure_minimum = pure_min,
      target_threshold = target,
      differences = diff_summary
    )
  })
  
  names(report) <- sections_order
  return(report)
}

# =============================================================================
# 4. Example Usage
# =============================================================================

# Create a dummy dataset. In your case, you already have a tibble with columns:
# "site_index", "sample_index", "site_name", "sum", "time_range", "geological_context",
# "number_of_individuals", "age", "gender", "accumulation_cause", "hominin_species",
# "bone.level", "element", "count"
example_data <- tibble(
  site_index = 1,
  sample_index = 1,
  site_name = "Example Site",
  sum = 10,
  time_range = "Late Pleistocene",
  geological_context = "Context1",
  number_of_individuals = 2,
  age = "Adult",
  gender = "M",
  accumulation_cause = "Predation",
  hominin_species = "Homo neanderthalensis",
  # For this example, the bone.level, element and count columns are list columns.
  bone.level = list(c(5, 1, 1, 3)),
  element = list(c("Skull_bone.Frontal", "Arm_bone.Humerus", "Arm_bone.Radius", "Arm_bone.Ulna")),
  count = list(c(1, 2, 2, 2))
)

# Define the order of sections you want to analyze. (Adjust as needed.)
sections_order <- c("Skull", "Arms", "Vertebrae", "Thorax", "Shoulder", 
                    "Hands", "Pelvic", "Legs", "Foot")

# Call the analysis function.
# Here, we set the target threshold to "Level A" which (by our rule) means one level above the minimum.
result <- analyze_bone_levels(example_data, sections_order, target_threshold = "Level A")

# Print the result.
print(result)

```

```{r}
# Load the necessary libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# =============================================================================
# 1. Prepare the Data: Unnest the List-Columns and Rename Them
# =============================================================================

prepare_bone_data <- function(data) {
  # Unnest the list columns so that each row corresponds to one bone record.
  # We assume that the columns "bone.level", "element", and "count" are lists.
  bone_data <- data %>%
    unnest(cols = c(bone.level, element, count))
  
  # Rename columns for clarity:
  bone_data <- bone_data %>%
    rename(
      hierarchical_level = bone.level,  # numeric level (e.g., 5, 1, 1, 3, …)
      bone_name = element               # bone name (e.g., "Skull_bone.Frontal")
    ) %>%
    # Ensure that count is numeric
    mutate(count = as.numeric(count))
  
  return(bone_data)
}

# =============================================================================
# 2. Summarize a Section: Group by Hierarchical Level and Bone Name
# =============================================================================

# Note: We change the function parameter to 'section_name' to avoid confusion.
summarize_section <- function(bone_data, section_name) {
  # Filter the data to include only bones in the specified section.
  section_data <- bone_data %>% filter(section == section_name)
  
  # Group by the numeric hierarchical_level and the bone name,
  # then sum the counts.
  level_summary <- section_data %>%
    group_by(hierarchical_level, bone_name) %>%
    summarise(total = sum(count, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')
  
  return(level_summary)
}

# =============================================================================
# 3. Main Analysis Function: Compare Pure Minimum Level to a Target Threshold
# =============================================================================

analyze_bone_levels <- function(data, sections_order, target_threshold = "Level A") {
  # Step 1: Prepare the data (unnest and rename columns)
  bone_data <- prepare_bone_data(data)
  
  # Step 2: Assign each bone to a section.
  # Adjust these pattern-matching rules according to your naming conventions.
  bone_data <- bone_data %>%
    mutate(section = case_when(
      grepl("Skull", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Skull",
      grepl("Humerus|Radius|Ulna", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Arms",
      grepl("Vertebra", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Vertebrae",
      grepl("Thorax", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Thorax",
      grepl("Shoulder", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Shoulder",
      grepl("Hand", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Hands",
      grepl("Pelvic", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Pelvic",
      grepl("Leg", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Legs",
      grepl("Foot", bone_name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Foot",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ))
  
  # Step 3: For each section in the provided order, get the summaries.
  report <- map(sections_order, function(sec) {
    sec_summary <- summarize_section(bone_data, sec)
    
    # If no records were found for the section, return a message:
    if(nrow(sec_summary) == 0) {
      return(list(
        section = sec,
        message = "No data for this section",
        pure_minimum = NULL,
        target_threshold = NULL,
        differences = NULL
      ))
    }
    
    # Determine the minimum hierarchical level (the pure minimum) for the section.
    # (We assume lower numeric values are more restrictive.)
    min_level <- min(as.numeric(sec_summary$hierarchical_level), na.rm = TRUE)
    
    # Determine the target threshold.
    # Here, if the user passes "Level A", we interpret it as one level above the minimum.
    target_thr <- if (is.character(target_threshold)) {
      if (target_threshold == "Level A") {
        min_level + 1
      } else {
        # For a string like "Level 3", remove "Level " and convert to numeric.
        as.numeric(gsub("Level ", "", target_threshold))
      }
    } else {
      # Otherwise assume the user provided a numeric value.
      target_threshold
    }
    
    # Get the summary at the pure minimum level.
    pure_min <- sec_summary %>% filter(as.numeric(hierarchical_level) == min_level)
    # And get the summary at the target threshold (if any data exist at that level).
    target <- sec_summary %>% filter(as.numeric(hierarchical_level) == target_thr)
    
    # Compute the differences: which bones are present at the target threshold but not at the pure minimum.
    diff_summary <- anti_join(target, pure_min, by = "bone_name")
    
    list(
      section = sec,
      pure_minimum = pure_min,
      target_threshold = target,
      differences = diff_summary
    )
  })
  
  names(report) <- sections_order
  return(report)
}

# =============================================================================
# 4. Example Usage
# =============================================================================

# Create a dummy dataset. In your case, you already have a tibble with these columns:
# "site_index", "sample_index", "site_name", "sum", "time_range", "geological_context",
# "number_of_individuals", "age", "gender", "accumulation_cause", "hominin_species",
# "bone.level", "element", "count"
example_data <- tibble(
  site_index = 1,
  sample_index = 1,
  site_name = "Example Site",
  sum = 10,
  time_range = "Late Pleistocene",
  geological_context = "Context1",
  number_of_individuals = 2,
  age = "Adult",
  gender = "M",
  accumulation_cause = "Predation",
  hominin_species = "Homo neanderthalensis",
  # In this example the three columns are list columns with one vector each.
  bone.level = list(c(5, 1, 1, 3)),
  element = list(c("Skull_bone.Frontal", "Arm_bone.Humerus", "Arm_bone.Radius", "Arm_bone.Ulna")),
  count = list(c(1, 2, 2, 2))
)

# Define the order of sections you want to analyze.
sections_order <- c("Skull", "Arms", "Vertebrae", "Thorax", "Shoulder", 
                    "Hands", "Pelvic", "Legs", "Foot")

# Call the analysis function.
# Here we set the target threshold to "Level A" which (by our rule) means one level above the minimum.
result <- analyze_bone_levels(example_data, sections_order, target_threshold = "Level A")

# Print the result.
print(result)
```
